sections.title: Adverse events monitoring as a routine component of vaccine clinical trials: evidence from the WHO Vaccine Trial Registry

summary.text: A 2000 Bulletin feedback piece reporting on how adverse events following immunization were monitored in vaccine trials recorded in the WHO Vaccine Trial Registry. It notes that early-phase trials are too small to detect rare side-effects, defines adverse events according to Good Clinical Practice guidelines, and reviews 68 trials of vaccines against diseases such as cholera, hepatitis B, measles and typhoid. A closing table classifies the adverse events monitored, from local and mild systemic reactions to death, by short-term versus long-term follow-up.
